paper.title: Establishing the importance of co-creation and self-efficacy in creative collaboration with artificial intelligence
paper.pdf_filename: McGuire Cremer Van de Cruys (2024) - Establishing the importance of co-creation and self-efficacy in creative collabo.pdf
paper.version_read: Published Scientific Reports journal version, (2024) 14:18525, DOI 10.1038/s41598-024-69423-2 (PDF p. 1); received 15 March 2024 and accepted 5 August 2024 (PDF p. 9).
paper.one_line_finding: Professional poets rated poems submitted by people who received an AI-generated poem to edit as less creative than poems written alone (Study 1: 12.55 vs 18.23 on a 1 to 40 scale, p < 0.001, p. 4 and Table 1; Study 2: 12.53 vs 15.74, p = 0.001, p. 6 and Table 2 on p. 7), while writing line by line in turns with the AI did not differ from writing alone (14.70 vs 15.74, p = 0.278) and scored higher than the editing condition (p = 0.026).

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Consensual Assessment Technique: 10 professional poets rated every poem relative to the other poems, on a 1 (lowest creativity) to 40 (highest creativity) scale, in separately randomized orders and without author or condition information (PDF pp. 3-4). One poem was submitted per participant. The paper does not specify how ratings were aggregated or report inter-rater reliability. ANOVA and post hoc LSD comparisons operate on poem scores; Table 1 supplies arm means and SDs.

estimates.notes: The reported analysis uses one score per poem; each person submitted one poem, so the human-arm SDs are also participant-level SDs and se_basis is participant. The full collection in the paper's three-group ANOVA contains 146 poems, including 50 AI-only benchmark poems outside this contrast (PDF p. 4). A separate poem total for the two human arms is not printed, so n_units is null under the no-computation rule. The printed participant counts remain n_treatment=48, n_control=48, and n_total=96 (PDF pp. 2 and 4). The post hoc LSD error term therefore includes the AI-only benchmark. The omnibus F and partial eta-squared are not pairwise effects. No pairwise test statistic, effect-size estimate, SE, or CI is printed. Study 1 recruitment/exclusion counts and the omnibus error degrees of freedom are internally inconsistent; see open_items.

not_extracted.reason: A self-reported belief about creative ability, not creativity or diversity scored on the poem (PDF pp. 5-6, Figure 3; PDF p. 7, Table 2).

not_extracted.what: Study 2: mediation analyses of expert creativity through creative self-efficacy, including direct and indirect paths for co-creator versus editor and human versus co-creator
not_extracted.reason: These are mechanism analyses conditional on a post-assignment self-report mediator. Their path coefficients, indirect effects, bootstrap SEs and CIs are not the full randomized total-effect contrasts extracted here. Direct-path coefficients are presented only in Figure 5 (PDF p. 7).

not_extracted.what: Studies 1 and 2: omnibus ANOVA statistics for expert-rated creativity
not_extracted.reason: The omnibus tests and partial eta-squared summarize all three conditions, rather than one eligible two-arm contrast. Study 1 also includes the AI-only benchmark. The eligible pairwise comparisons are extracted from arm summaries and the explicitly reported post hoc p-values (PDF p. 4, Study 1; PDF p. 6, Expert evaluations of creativity).

open_items: Study 1 (PDF p. 2) prints 101 recruited, six attention-check exclusions, and 96 remaining, with 48 people in each human arm. These counts do not reconcile. Timing and arm allocation of exclusions are unstated, so randomized counts remain null.

Study 1 (PDF p. 4) prints 146 poems in the expert-rating analysis but reports omnibus F(2, 145) = 63.48, p < 0.001, partial η2 = 0.47. The error degrees of freedom conflict with the stated three-group analysis. The post hoc error term also includes 50 AI-only poems. No correction is inferred.

Study 2 human-arm expert-creativity SD conflicts: 4.98 in Table 2 (PDF p. 7) versus 9.24 in the narrative (PDF p. 6). The extracted control SD follows Table 2; the text discrepancy remains documented.

Study 2 co-creator versus human p-value is explicitly 0.278 (PDF p. 6), but the same paragraph includes p = 0.280 after the co-creator mean and SD without identifying a comparator. The explicit comparison is used.
Neither study explains aggregation of the professional poets' ratings or prints inter-rater reliability (PDF pp. 3-5). The arm SDs refer to poem scores, with one poem per participant in human arms.

Neither study prints numerical SEs or CIs for the total pairwise creativity contrasts. Study 2 Figure 4 has CI bars and difference annotations, but figure-only values are not extracted. No missing statistics or counts were calculated.

The paper does not report how many editor-arm participants edited the supplied AI poem or the extent of editing (PDF p. 3). The assigned access contrast includes the option of submitting the supplied poem unchanged.
Participant country and preregistration are not stated. The paper and screening form identify no other paper sharing either participant sample.
